styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Grand-Place, comic-strip murals and the old centre on foot.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Waffles, fries, chocolate and mussels between sights.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Magritte, Old Masters and the comic-strip museum.

stays.why: Steps from the main square, waffle stands and the station. Noisiest and busiest area; book early.
Quiet, elegant streets with antique shops, chocolate makers and the Fine Arts museum nearby.
Local feel, good bars and restaurants, easy tram rides to the centre. Good value.
Close to the EU buildings and parks; quiet on weekends. About 20 minutes by metro to the centre.

food: Try Belgian classics: moules-frites, carbonnade (beef stew with beer) and waterzooi. Main dishes often €15–25.
Waffles come two ways: dense Liège-style and lighter Brussels-style. Street stalls charge about €3–6; sit-down cafés cost more.
Fries from a fritkot (chip stand) with mayonnaise are a local habit, roughly €3–5 a cone.
Chocolate and pralines: compare small makers around Grand-Place and Sablon. Prices vary widely; check the label for cocoa content.
Beer cafés serve hundreds of Belgian beers. Ask for a small tasting glass if you are unsure; strong beers are often 8–12%.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for a half-day trip to Bruges or Ghent by train; check times and prices on the day.
Add the Atomium and Mini-Europe in the north if you want a break from the old centre.
Spend an extra morning at the Royal Museum of Fine Arts and the Magritte Museum in Sablon.

recommend.why: Two nights cover Grand-Place, the museums and a relaxed food day; add a third for a day trip to Bruges or Ghent.

month_notes: January: cold and grey, highs near 6°C, about 14 rain days. Pack a warm coat and waterproof shoes.
February: still cold, highs around 8°C, slightly fewer rain days. Museums are quiet.
March: cool at 11°C with about 14 rain days. Bring layers and an umbrella.
April: milder at 14°C, about 11 rain days. Good for walking the centre.
May: pleasant at 18°C, around 12 rain days. Terrace season begins.
June: warm at 22°C, about 10 rain days. Long evenings; book hotels early.
July: warmest month, highs near 23°C, about 11 rain days. Busy with tourists.
August: similar warmth, about 12 rain days. Many locals are away; some small shops close.
September: mild at 20°C, about 11 rain days. A comfortable month for sightseeing.
October: cooler at 16°C, about 13 rain days. Carry a rain jacket.
November: cold and wet, highs near 10°C, about 14 rain days. Short days; plan indoor sights.
December: cold at 8°C, about 14 rain days. Christmas markets and lights around Grand-Place.

climate_guide.summary: Temperate and often cloudy: mild summers, cool winters and rain in every month.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Highs of 18–23°C and the most daylight. Ideal for walking the centre and sitting outside.

items.title: Rain all year
items.text: Expect 10–14 rain days every month. Showers are often short; carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Cool winters
items.text: December to February highs of 6–8°C and lows near 2°C. A warm coat and layers are essential.

items.title: Mild, not hot, summers
items.text: July and August peak near 23°C. Rarely very hot; evenings can still feel cool.

items.title: Grey skies are common
items.text: Overcast days are frequent. Plan museums and cafés as backups to outdoor plans.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers, a waterproof jacket and comfortable shoes for cobblestones. Add a scarf and gloves in winter.

transit.best: Walk the compact centre; use metro or tram for longer hops.

modes.text: STIB/MIVB metro and trams reach most sights. A single ride costs about €2.10–2.60; tap a contactless bank card or buy a MOBIB card (about €6) for cheaper fares.
STIB buses cover the city. De Lijn buses serve the airport and Flanders, but their tickets are not valid on STIB.
Uber, Bolt and local taxi apps work. Taxis from the airport cost around €60.
Driving is slow and parking is costly. A low-emission zone covers the centre; check your car meets the rules.
The centre is compact and walkable. Shared bikes and scooters are common for longer trips.
